sources.title: Mueller report timeline: what it says about Trump and Russia

supported_event_claim: Mueller investigation records quote Corsi's August 2, 2016 email to Stone about two anticipated WikiLeaks releases and a proposed Clinton cognitive-decline attack.
reason: Primary-source email quoted in detailed reporting; supports the communication, not the truth of its claims or Stone's response.

sources.title: Senate Select Committee on Intelligence, Volume 5

supported_event_claim: The Senate Intelligence Committee found Manafort shared internal campaign polling data with Kilimnik in August 2016.
reason: Official bipartisan committee report documents the event; does not establish that Kilimnik was an intelligence agent.
No credible source located establishing that Stone physically dined with Assange on this date; reporting concerns Stone's disputed claims of contact, not a verified dinner.

sources.title: Ex-CIA Chief Calls Trump 'Unwitting Agent' Of Russia, Endorses Clinton

supported_event_claim: Former CIA director Michael Morell publicly called Trump an unwitting agent of Russia in an opinion piece and endorsed Clinton.
reason: Contemporaneous report precisely attributes the phrase as Morell's opinion, not a government finding.

sources.title: Senate Select Committee on Intelligence, Volume 5

supported_event_claim: The committee found Trump and campaign officials sought advance information about WikiLeaks releases and believed Stone had inside information.
reason: Official investigation supports the broad campaign knowledge and communications; exact date in the packet is not established as the moment Trump first learned of emails.

sources.title: Trump says gun-rights supporters can do something to stop Clinton

supported_event_claim: At a 2016 rally Trump said that Second Amendment supporters might be able to stop Clinton's judicial appointments; the remark was widely interpreted as violent innuendo.
reason: Contemporaneous reporting gives the statement in context; it does not establish an explicit call to kill Clinton.
Could not locate reliable evidence for the claimed Croatia vacation and meeting with a Russian oligarch on this date; available reporting does not establish that combined event.

sources.title: Meet the conservative operatives running Trump's campaign

supported_event_claim: Trump's campaign announced Steve Bannon as chief executive and Kellyanne Conway as campaign manager.
reason: Contemporaneous reporting documents the personnel announcement.
Sources located document Stone-Bannon communications about WikiLeaks in October, not the specific August 18 event alleged in the packet.
Could not locate credible contemporaneous evidence that Prince Alwaleed said he saved Trump from bankruptcy; the specific attributed quote remains unsubstantiated.

sources.title: FBI's James Comey: We take election hacking 'very seriously'

supported_event_claim: By August 30, Reid had sent Comey a letter urging investigation of alleged Russian election tampering.
reason: Contemporaneous report confirms the letter, but does not substantiate the packet's exact August 27 date.
No direct credible source located for the specific September 9 warning as stated in the packet; a general opinion or prediction would not verify the event.

sources.title: New York Attorney General investigating Trump Foundation

supported_event_claim: New York Attorney General Eric Schneiderman announced an investigation into the Trump Foundation's fundraising and charitable activities.
reason: Contemporaneous report documents the investigation announcement; does not prejudge illegality.
The September 28 House hearing listed DHS, Election Assistance Commission, Georgia, and academic witnesses, not FBI Director Comey; the attributed testimony is unsupported.

sources.title: Joint DHS and ODNI statement on election security
sources.publisher: National Security Archive, George Washington University

supported_event_claim: DHS and ODNI publicly stated that the U.S. intelligence community was confident the Russian government directed compromises of political organizations and disclosures.
reason: Archived copy of the official joint statement; supports public attribution, not the packet's counterfactual that it was futile.
The packet's claim that Stone ordered WikiLeaks to release emails that day is an allegation from later reporting and is not established by a contemporaneous direct source.

sources.title: Trump Taj Mahal closes after 26 years

supported_event_claim: The Trump Taj Mahal casino in Atlantic City closed on October 10, 2016.
reason: Contemporaneous reporting confirms the closure; the packet's characterization of Icahn's ownership timing is not needed to support this event.

sources.title: Trump Jr. met with Russian officials in Paris during campaign

supported_event_claim: Reporting said Trump Jr. received a speaking fee of at least $50,000 for a Paris appearance attended by Russian officials in 2016.
reason: Credible retrospective reporting supports the reported fee and appearance; 'Russian assets' is not established and is not repeated as fact.

sources.title: Senate Select Committee on Intelligence, Volume 5

supported_event_claim: The Senate report documents GRU-controlled Guccifer 2.0 outreach to journalists and media figures, including unsuccessful attempts to contact Alex Jones.
reason: Official investigation documents the broader contact effort; precise October 18 timing is not confirmed in the cited material.

sources.title: Documents Point to Illegal Campaign Coordination Between Trump and NRA

supported_event_claim: The Trace reported the NRA spent about $30 million supporting Trump and presented documents suggesting coordinated ad buying; the FEC response rejected key coordination allegations in the cited complaint.
reason: Sources establish the spending and contested allegation, not an adjudicated finding of illegal coordination.

sources.title: Read the Full Transcript of the Third Presidential Debate

supported_event_claim: During the third presidential debate Clinton said Putin would rather have a puppet as president and Trump replied, 'No puppet.'
reason: Debate transcript directly records the exchange.

sources.title: Document: Justice Department Releases Carter Page FISA Application

supported_event_claim: The released redacted application shows the FBI sought a FISA warrant for Carter Page on October 21, 2016; it contains the FBI's stated belief about Page's collaboration with Russia.
reason: Direct document reproduction with context; the packet's wording 'likely Russian operative' is an interpretation, not a formal designation.

sources.title: Michael Cohen Pleads Guilty in Manhattan Federal Court to Eight Counts
sources.publisher: U.S. Attorney's Office, Southern District of New York

supported_event_claim: Cohen admitted arranging and funding a $130,000 payment to a woman identified in court documents as Individual-2 shortly before the 2016 election.
reason: Official plea record supports the payment arrangement; it does not establish that the 2016 transfer itself was adjudicated illegal or that Trump Jr. signed the transfer.

sources.title: Statement by FBI Director James B. Comey on the Use of Additional Investigative Steps

supported_event_claim: Comey notified Congress that the FBI was reviewing additional emails potentially relevant to the Clinton email investigation.
reason: The letter is primary evidence; the claim that Comey intended to mislead voters is not established by it.

sources.title: DOJ OIG Review of FBI Records Vault Twitter Announcements
sources.publisher: U.S. Department of Justice, Office of Inspector General

supported_event_claim: The FBI Records Vault account issued 20 backlog tweets on October 30, 2016, including one about Fred Trump; OIG attributed the backlog to a technical malfunction and found no evidence of deliberate political timing.
reason: Official OIG investigation directly addresses the incident and contradicts the packet's infiltration framing.
